items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee addresses 'Milt' directly in the transcript (e.g., 'Milt, you haven't tasted no meat yet...', 'Milt, I had such great musicians...'), indicating familiarity, but no specific professional or personal relationship (like collaboration, mentorship, or friendship) is described in the prov

ctx.x: Because they had the money to buy a saxophone.

Right. Yeah, because my mother was doing work, and I used to... I delivered many a bundle of laundry. We had a horse... Man, when I think of it, we was loaded! We had a horse, we had chickens, hogs... And my grandfather used to come in every Fall and help kill the hogs. And he had a smokehouse... Milt, you haven't tasted no meat yet until you taste how he smoked that meat. And he knew how to make syrup out of cane... My grandfather was... He grew the best okra. He was a farmer at heart, but he was just a…
And that's how we got along. Because actually, my mother had them big pots where she would wash the clothes, put the clothes in there and soak it and all that...

items.q: And then I had them get a New York bass player and let him sub and do the best he can

ctx.x: And then I had them get a New York bass player and let him sub and do the best he can until, you know, you get your card.
I had been in the band almost six months on the road by the time I got there.
